headline_marked: Record $6.3bn theft: [[Binance hit by largest-known crypto hack]]
headline: Record $6.3bn theft: Binance hit by largest-known crypto hack
summary: Analysts link the massive security breach to North Korea, as the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange halts withdrawals to cover losses.
details: Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a record-breaking theft. The heist unfolded in approximately 20 minutes starting late Thursday, causing cryptocurrency prices to fall broadly.

Blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis have attributed the attack to North Korea’s elite hacking unit. They noted similarities to a previous 2025 heist at the Bybit exchange attributed to Pyongyang.
Binance stated the breach may have begun with a compromised laptop belonging to one of its engineers. This allowed attackers to gain system access and execute unauthorized withdrawals.
The exchange has halted withdrawals and co-CEO Richard Teng assured users that their funds are safe and that Binance will cover every loss.
About $3 billion of the stolen assets have been located and frozen by stablecoin issuers including Tether, Circle, and World Liberty Financial.
North Korea has routinely denied allegations of state-linked cyber theft, and its diplomatic missions did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
caption:
The largest crypto hack in history. $6.3 billion vanished in just 20 minutes.

Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a record-breaking theft. The heist unfolded in approximately 20 minutes starting late Thursday, causing cryptocurrency prices to fall broadly.

Blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis have attributed the attack to North Korea’s elite hacking unit. They noted similarities to a previous 2025 heist at the Bybit exchange attributed to Pyongyang.

Binance stated the breach may have begun with a compromised laptop belonging to one of its engineers. This allowed attackers to gain system access and execute unauthorized withdrawals.

The exchange has halted withdrawals and co-CEO Richard Teng assured users that their funds are safe and that Binance will cover every loss.

About $3 billion of the stolen assets have been located and frozen by stablecoin issuers including Tether, Circle, and World Liberty Financial.

North Korea has routinely denied allegations of state-linked cyber theft, and its diplomatic missions did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

headline_marked: Dengue toll hits 418, [[third-highest annual death toll]] since 2000
headline: Dengue toll hits 418, third-highest annual death toll since 2000
summary: Three more people died yesterday, while 1,262 were hospitalized in 24 hours as health experts warn of critical complications and diagnostic delays.
details: Three more dengue-related deaths were reported yesterday, bringing this year's total to 418. This marks the third-highest annual death toll since Bangladesh first recorded an outbreak in 2000.

According to the DGHS, the highest number of deaths occurred in 2023 with 1,705, followed by 575 in 2024. A review of 119 patients found that over one-third died within 24 hours of being admitted to the hospital.

Dengue shock syndrome was identified as the leading cause of death at 62.5 percent, followed by expanded dengue syndrome at 31.2 percent. Many patients also experienced diagnostic delays of at least three days.

Medical professionals report a rise in severe complications this year, including liver, kidney, respiratory, and heart failure. Some experts suggest the circulation of dengue virus serotype 3 (DENV-3) may be contributing to the severity.

Public health expert Mushtuq Hussain described the rising toll as a failure of healthcare policy. He called for a shift toward community-level interventions and free testing at primary healthcare facilities.

Doctors warn that repeat infections and delays in seeking medical help increase vulnerability. They urge anyone with fever and body aches to seek immediate testing rather than waiting for conditions to worsen.
